articles.title: Italy unleashes military response to violent riots as France faces a reckoning of its own
articles.summary: Videos show police forced to retreat as rioters overwhelm officers in Paris and Milan, prompting France and Italy to announce military deployments.
articles.body:
Italy is moving to deploy 500 troops with expanded police powers following a weekend of violent riots, taking a more direct military approach to public security than France, where weeks of unrest have prompted authorities to bolster their security response.

Videos of unrest in France and Italy flooded social media on Saturday and Sunday, showing violent clashes between demonstrators and police amid burning buildings and looted storefronts. At multiple points during the chaos, police attempting to contain the violence were forced to retreat.

In Paris, for instance, roughly a dozen officers confronted several hundred demonstrators but were unable to make arrests, using rubber-bullet launchers and grenades to keep advancing rioters at bay as they made a gradual retreat. Italian police in Milan, meanwhile, made a similar retreat as hundreds of young rioters threw explosive firecrackers, metal barriers and glass bottles at them in their attempt to occupy a public square.

Though France is escalating its response now, demonstrations have been ongoing in the country since last month, with many schools being burned and ransacked by rioters.

A Fox News Digital investigation found that socialist groups , Islamic advocacy organizations and environmental activists were involved in the French riots, which financial analysts estimate caused over $1 billion in damages. Videos from the unrest also showed demonstrators waving foreign flags, including Palestinian flags in France and an Albanian flag during the violence in Milan.

Italian media reported that many first and second-generation migrants were among the rioters in Milan.

With another wave of riots planned for this coming weekend and authorities bracing for more violence, France and Italy are turning to their armed forces to reinforce security after days of rioting.

France's gendarmes, essentially military police officers, assisted in containing last weekend's riots . The nation's interior minister announced on Tuesday that the military would be increasing its presence in anticipation of further rioting.

"We will ⁠deploy the Sentinelle force, ​obviously ‌as a substitute ‌to interior security ‌forces ... mostly to free police and gendarmes in their mission to maintain order," he ‌told France's legislature.

France has upcoming presidential elections, with some political observers viewing the migrant-heavy riots as an electoral boon for Marine Le Pen, the most popular right-wing candidate.

Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni announced a similar deployment, pledging that 500 troops will be entering Milan. The country's deputy prime minister explained that the police would be granted police powers, providing some insight into the role they could play in squaring off against rioters.

articles.title: Ministros do TSE discutiram bloqueio de canais políticos no WhatsApp às vésperas da eleição | G1
articles.standfirst: Texto prevê equiparar regras de proibição para impulsionamento de conteúdo aos canais. André Mendonça ficou responsável por elaborar proposta, mas resolução não deve avançar, segundo ministros da Corte.
articles.summary: Texto prevê equiparar regras de proibição para impulsionamento de conteúdo aos canais. André Mendonça ficou responsável por elaborar proposta, mas resolução não deve avançar, segundo ministros da Corte.
articles.body:
O presidente do Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE), Kassio Nunes Marques , e o vice-presidente da Corte, André Mendonça , discutiram com colegas a possibilidade de impor restrições a canais de WhatsApp com mais de 200 mil usuários nas 48 horas anteriores ao segundo turno das eleições, no próximo domingo (25).

A proposta, que foi debatida nos últimos dias e dividiu a Corte, atingiria canais como o "Exército do Lula" , que conta com quase 8 milhões de seguidores, e o canal "Tropa do Flávio", que tem 2,7 milhões.

Nas últimas semanas, o canal de mensagens liderado pelo deputado federal André Janones (Rede-MG) gerou embates no cenário político do segundo turno e virou alvo de disputas judiciais entre as campanhas (relembre mais abaixo).

Em nota, o gabinete do ministro André Mendonça informou que os integrantes da Corte discutiram o tema em duas reuniões, realizadas na sexta-feira (16) e na terça-feira (20), e coube ao ministro elaborar uma minuta de resolução, que seria submetida para a avaliação dos demais.

À TV Globo , Nunes Marques afirmou não ser "favorável a mudança de última hora". A resolução não deve avançar, segundo informações de outros ministros da Corte.

A nota do gabinete afirma que, "por tradição, cabe ao vice-presidente do Tribunal redigir os atos normativos que o colegiado vai apreciar. Era natural, portanto, que essa tarefa coubesse ao Ministro André Mendonça. A minuta não é uma iniciativa individual".

O texto prossegue: "A necessidade de sua elaboração parte de um entendimento construído em conjunto, o texto ainda está em discussão interna, e qualquer versão final depende de deliberação colegiada do Tribunal".

O gabinete também afirma que "nessas reuniões, houve consenso entre todos os ministros sobre a necessidade de tratar do assunto".

E que o objetivo "é proteger a integridade do pleito nas horas que antecedem e sucedem a votação, quando não há tempo hábil para resposta ou correção de conteúdos ilícitos" .

A resolução em debate previa equiparar regras de proibição para impulsionamento de conteúdo aos canais.

🔎Conforme as regras da Justiça Eleitoral, o impulsionamento pago de propaganda eleitoral na internet é permitido até 22 de outubro. A partir do dia 23, a prática fica proibida, inclusive para conteúdos contratados anteriormente. A restrição vale até 26 de outubro.

O texto da resolução, à qual a TV Globo teve acesso, diz o seguinte: "No período compreendido entre as 48 horas antes e as 24 horas depois da eleição, aplica-se o disposto no § 11 deste artigo aos canais de transmissão de conteúdo de natureza político-eleitoral com mais de 200.000 (duzentos mil) seguidores".

Segundo o texto, "consideram-se canais de transmissão de conteúdo de natureza político-eleitoral, o canal, grupo, comunidade ou lista de transmissão em aplicativo de mensagens instantâneas ou em plataforma digital, inclusive de transmissão ao vivo, de acesso aberto ou mediante convite, que transmita conteúdo de natureza político-eleitoral, em especial aqueles informados à Justiça Eleitoral pelas campanhas, os administrados por candidatos, partidos, federações e detentores de mandato eletivo".

A campanha do candidato à reeleição Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) oficializou em 13 de outubro o registro do endereço eletrônico do canal de WhatsApp conhecido como "Exército do Lula" no Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE).

O registro ocorreu após uma série de impasses e embates jurídicos que o canal de WhatsApp enfrentou na Justiça Eleitoral.

O vaivém começou após a campanha de Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) pedir a suspensão do canal por suposta divulgação de informações falsas.

O ministro Nunes Marques, presidente da Corte Eleitoral, determinou a suspensão do canal. Horas depois, o corregedor-geral eleitoral, Ricardo Villas Bôas Cueva, decidiu manter a página ativa, contrariando a decisão de Nunes Marques.

O ministro, então, determinou que a equipe técnica do TSE fizesse uma análise do canal. Como resultado, o relatório não encontrou conteúdos falsos nas publicações examinadas que estavam no ar.

Nunes Marques então condicionou o funcionamento do canal o registro formal na Justiça Eleitoral, exigência que foi cumprida pela campanha de Lula (PT).

articles.title: Horário eleitoral: Flávio foca em mulheres e Lula cita Santos Cruz | G1
articles.standfirst: Petista destacou obras do Novo PAC e propostas em infraestrutura; candidato do PL retomou propostas para mulheres e exibiu trechos do debate da Band com críticas à fala de Lula sobre saidinhas e imagens de atos de apoio.
articles.summary: No horário eleitoral, Lula criticou cortes em programas sociais e exibiu Santos Cruz, enquanto Flávio Bolsonaro repetiu propostas para mulheres e segurança.
articles.body:
Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) e Lula (PT) durante o horário eleitoral gratuito dessa quarta-feira (21). — Foto: Reprodução

No horário eleitoral gratuito desta quarta-feira (21), Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) retomou peças exibidas anteriormente, com propostas voltadas às mulheres, trechos do debate presidencial e imagens de manifestações de apoiadores. Já Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT), candidato à reeleição, fez críticas ao plano de cortes de gastos anunciado pelo adversário, chamado de "tesouraço", e destacou propostas para a infraestrutura.

Primeira a ser exibida, a propaganda de Flávio voltou a destacar as propostas do "Brasil por Elas", plano voltado às mulheres. O candidato defendeu a redução da maioridade penal e sugeriu que, se Lula for reeleito, a regra não será alterada.

Na peça, o candidato também conversou com uma beneficiária do Bolsa Família e prometeu manter o programa. Entre as propostas reapresentadas estavam criar centros de atendimento para crianças com autismo e um vale-creche.

A propaganda também retomou críticas à saída temporária de presos, a saidinha, em uma fala de Lula durante o debate na TV Bandeirantes no último domingo (18). Ao final, Flávio reexibiu atos a favor dele pelo Brasil, com depoimentos de aliados políticos.

Em peça inédita, o programa de Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) criticou o “tesouraço” proposto por Flávio e sugeriu que o adversário, se eleito, vai cortar benefícios sociais, como Bolsa Família, Pé-de-Meia e Farmácia Popular.

O petista também destacou obras do Novo PAC, investimentos em infraestrutura, geração de empregos e valorização do salário mínimo. O programa comparou as propostas do atual governo às medidas adotadas durante a gestão de Jair Bolsonaro (PL), pai de Flávio, e mencionou obras paralisadas.

Em outro trecho da propaganda, o vice-presidente Geraldo Alckmin (PSB) afirmou que não é necessário ser petista para votar em Lula. A propaganda exibiu depoimentos de aliados do presidente e terminou com um trecho de uma entrevista do general Santos Cruz, ex-ministro de Bolsonaro, ao canal "Revelando' no YouTube, em que o militar criticou Jair e Flávio Bolsonaro.

articles.title: Pesquisa Quaest: Economia é o maior desafio do próximo presidente | G1
articles.standfirst: Combate à violência e ao crime aparece em segundo lugar, com 13%; economia lidera entre eleitores de Flávio, enquanto entre os de Lula as prioridades ficam mais divididas
articles.summary: Pesquisa Quaest aponta o crescimento econômico como o principal desafio do próximo presidente para 21% dos brasileiros, seguido pelo combate à violência.
articles.body:
O crescimento da economia e a saída da crise são a prioridade mais citada pelos brasileiros para quem assumir o Palácio do Planalto em 2027.

Segundo pesquisa Quaest divulgada nesta quarta-feira (21) encomendada pela Globo e pelo jornal O Globo, 21% dos eleitores afirmam que esse deve ser o principal desafio do próximo presidente, “seja ele quem for”.

O segundo desafio mais relatado é o combate a violência e o crime, com 13%.

📋A Quaest entrevistou 2.154 pessoas de 16 anos ou mais, entre os dias 17 e 20 de outubro. A margem de erro é de dois pontos percentuais, para mais ou para menos, e o nível de confiança é de 95%. A pesquisa está registrada como BR-08535/2026.

articles.title: Flávio Bolsonaro impõe condições a Lula para abrir sigilos no TSE | G1
articles.standfirst: Defesa do candidato do PL exige que Lula inclua na quebra de sigilos contas de ex-assessores, dados de cartões corporativos e registros de reuniões no Palácio do Planalto.
articles.summary: Flávio Bolsonaro pede ao TSE que Lula inclua dados de ex-assessores, cartões corporativos e registros do Planalto na quebra de sigilos bancário e fiscal.
articles.body:
O candidato à Presidência pelo PL , senador Flávio Bolsonaro , apresentou nesta terça-feira (21) uma petição no Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE) em resposta ao desafio de quebras de sigilo lançado nesta semana pelo presidente e candidato à reeleição , Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva ( PT ).

No documento, endereçado ao ministro André Mendonça , Flávio diz aceitar abrir seus sigilos bancário, fiscal e telefônico dos últimos 20 anos , além de dados de seus familiares citados e de empresas de sua propriedade.

No entanto, como condição para isso, impõe que o petista faça o mesmo, ampliando os objetos das quebras de sigilos ( leia mais aqui ).

Na véspera, Lula havia protocolado um documento no TSE declarando "autorizar" a abertura de seus sigilos e de seus familiares nos últimos 8 anos, condicionando o ato à reciprocidade do adversário.

Para a defesa de Flávio Bolsonaro, no entanto, a proposta inicial de Lula seria uma "promessa vazia" e uma "quebra para inglês ver", argumentando que eventuais irregularidades do adversário estariam ocultas em nomes de terceiros, laranjas e empresas, e não em suas contas diretas.

"O pedido de Lula é uma verdadeira aberração jurídica. Não pede nada ao Tribunal, não se encaixa em nenhum tipo de processo e depende da vontade de quem nem sequer é parte. Também é desnecessário, porque, caso o candidato estivesse realmente preocupado em levar a verdade aos eleitores, poderia, ele próprio, divulgar os extratos", afirmam os advogados na peça.

Na petição apresentada no TSE, o senador condiciona o levantamento de dados a exigências que abrangem tanto o período em que Lula exerceu mandatos anteriores quanto a atual gestão federal. Entre as principais exigências feitas pela campanha de Flávio Bolsonaro estão:

Sigilos de assessores próximos : apresentação de termos de autorização de quebra de sigilo de assessores, como Marco Aurélio Santana Ribeiro, o "Marcola", ex-chefe de gabinete .

Empresas de familiares e sócios : abertura de contas e sigilos de empresas ligadas a familiares do presidente, incluindo sociedades do filho Fábio Luís Lula da Silva, o "Lulinha" , negócios recentes no exterior, empresas de outros filhos, além do Instituto Lula e da empresa L.I.L.S. Palestras desde o ano de 2003 .

Caso Master : divulgação integral de registros de visitantes no Palácio do Planalto e detalhes da reunião mantida entre Lula e Daniel Vorcaro em dezembro de 2024.

INSS : esclarecimentos sobre as relações do governo com a lobista Roberta Luchsinger, registros de suas entradas em palácios presidenciais e voos na Força Aérea Brasileira (FAB), e a quebra de sigilo do sindicalista Frei Chico, irmão de Lula.

Cartão corporativo : abertura de todos os gastos do cartão corporativo da Presidência da República desde janeiro de 2023, e de agendas institucionais da primeira-dama, Janja , desde o primeiro ano de mandato.

Na petição, Flávio Bolsonaro diz que "quem não deve, não recorta" e que o pedido feito por Lula, às vésperas do segundo turno, exige transparência total. Ele também critica o que classifica como um "factóide" da campanha do petista.

O candidato do PL pede ainda que o TSE intime Lula a dizer se aceita as condições e, em caso negativo, que seja registrado no processo que o petista recusou a proposta.

Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) e Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) — Foto: Montagem/g1, Reprodução/Divulgação das campanhas

Flávio nega ser sócio de Tomaz em empresa

No documento enviado ao TSE, Flávio diz que não é sócio, administrador nem beneficiário da Alcazar Holdings, empresa do advogado e amigo do candidato do PL Willer Tomaz.

Flávio diz que, por isso, não tem dados bancários e fiscais da empresa.

Flávio Bolsonaro foi cadastrado como "usuário master" de uma conta bancária pertencente à referida empresa de Willer Tomaz, investigado por suspeita de lavagem de dinheiro. Nesta terça-feira (20), Lula defendeu a quebra dos sigilos da Alcazar Holdings.

Flávio é alvo de dois inquéritos em tramitação no Supremo Tribunal Federal ( STF ). Um deles, sobre lavagem de dinheiro, investiga a relação do candidato do PL com o advogado Willer Tomaz.

O outro inquérito trata do financiamento de "Dark Horse", uma cinebiografia sobre Jair Bolsonaro. Essa investigação apura negociações envolvendo recursos do banqueiro Daniel Vorcaro, do Banco Master, para a produção do filme.

A defesa do senador tem negado irregularidades nas investigações, afirmando que não há envolvimento em ilícitos e criticando a divulgação de peças sigilosas durante o período eleitoral.

articles.title: Pesquisa Quaest: Para 69% dos brasileiros, renda cresceu no último ano | G1
articles.standfirst: Para 32% dos que afirmaram que a renda aumentou, ela subiu na mesma proporção que o custo de vida; para 21%, menos; e para 16%, mais. Outros 28% dizem que a renda não aumentou no período.
articles.summary: Pesquisa Quaest revela que 69% da população percebeu aumento de renda, com 16% dos entrevistados afirmando que os ganhos superaram o custo de vida no último ano.
articles.body:
A percepção dos brasileiros sobre o próprio poder de compra mudou no mês de outubro, segundo pesquisa Quaest divulgada nesta quarta-feira (21) encomendada pela Globo e pelo jornal O Globo . Para 16% dos entrevistados, a renda da família aumentou mais que o custo de vida no último ano. É o maior índice desde março, início da série. Entre agosto e setembro, esse grupo estava estável em 10%.

Na direção oposta, os que dizem que a renda não aumentou oscilou negativamente para 28%, o menor patamar da série. Eram 35% em junho e 32% na semana passada. A resposta mais frequente agora é que a renda acompanhou os preços (32%). Outros 21% afirmam que ela subiu menos que a inflação.

Renda aumentou tanto quanto o custo de vida: 32% (era 29% em 14 de outubro);

Renda aumentou menos que custo de vida: 21% (era 23%);

articles.title: Eleição acirrada vira palco de promessas que aumentam pressão sobre as contas públicas | G1
articles.body:
A eleição presidencial mais acirrada dos últimos tempos virou palco de promessas dos dois lados que podem pressionar ainda mais as contas públicas caso sejam de fato cumpridas.

Quem vencer a disputa, portanto, terá um desafio imediato: seja o senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), seja o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT), terá de encontrar recursos para cumprir o que prometeu ou rever parte dos compromissos de campanha para evitar um desequilíbrio ainda maior nas contas públicas.

O presidente Lula enfileirou uma série de medidas durante a eleição que poderão chegar a mais de R$ 283 bilhões em impacto fiscal e financeiro .

A equipe econômica garante que o valor será compensado no Orçamento da União de 2027 e que a maior parte das medidas não terá impacto imediato nas contas públicas ( entenda mais abaixo ).

Apenas uma delas, o aumento do Bolsa Família, poderá ter custo de mais de 23,2 bilhões para a União no primeiro ano do mandato do próximo presidente, segundo levantamento de consultoria especializada.

O candidato do PL, Flávio Bolsonaro, decidiu entrar na onda. Nos últimos dias, prometeu o "Vira Pix", com a devolução aos contribuintes de parte do que pagam em suas contas , sem definir de onde sairão os recursos.

Também prometeu retomar o programa de incentivo ao setor cultural — o Programa Emergencial de Retomada do Setor de Eventos (Perse) — desativado pelo atual governo por causa do alto custo e de desvios de finalidade.

O fato é que, se um ajuste fiscal no próximo ano já se fazia necessário, agora ele se tornou praticamente inevitável.

Sem cortes de despesas, principalmente de investimentos, os ministérios poderão ficar sem recursos básicos para manter a máquina funcionando, e vários programas poderão ser paralisados.

Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) e Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) — Foto: Montagem/g1, Reprodução/Divulgação das campanhas

A avaliação de especialistas em contas públicas é que o próximo governo poderá enfrentar um início de mandato muito difícil: ou promoverá um grande ajuste, ou os juros poderão continuar elevados para conter a inflação.

O economista-chefe e sócio da Warren Investimentos, Felipe Salto, aponta os riscos que as promessas dos candidatos podem representar para o próximo governo.

“É preocupante que tanto Lula quanto Flávio estejam protagonizando espécie de race to the bottom, com essas promessas e ações. Fala-se em ressuscitar o Perse e perdoar dívidas, no caso de Flávio, criam-se programas para o MEI [microempreendedor individual], promete-se tarifa zero etc., no caso de Lula. Quem paga a conta?”, diz Salto.

Segundo ele, os cálculos de sua equipe indicam que o impacto no próximo ano pode chegar perto de R$ 48 bilhões.

Para Salto, “o modo gastar foi ativado pelo presidente Lula, ainda que opere dentro das regras do jogo”, e Flávio Bolsonaro entrou na roda.

O resultado, segundo o economista, é que o movimento dos dois candidatos deverá aumentar a pressão fiscal em 2027.

“Na verdade, são vendas de terrenos na Lua, que terão de ser revistas seja qual for o resultado da eleição. O Orçamento, ainda nem apreciado pelo Congresso, já continha receita inflada e, mesmo assim, não seria possível cumprir a meta de superávit indicada. Agora, as coisas se complicaram ainda mais”, conclui Felipe Salto.

Na proposta de Orçamento enviada ao Congresso, o governo estabeleceu meta de superávit primário de R$ 73,2 bilhões em 202 7, equivalente a 0,5% do PIB. A própria equipe econômica, porém, projeta um resultado positivo menor, de R$ 18,6 bilhões.

A Instituição Fiscal Independente (IFI), órgão ligado ao Senado, faz uma projeção mais pessimista e estima déficit de R$ 86,1 bilhões em 2027 . O cálculo foi feito antes do anúncio do reajuste do Bolsa Família.

articles.title: Fio do Professor Felipe Nunes: análise da pesquisa Quaest para presidente de 21 de outubro | G1
articles.standfirst: Diretor da Quaest e professor da Fundação Getúlio Vargas (FGV), Felipe Nunes avalia momento atual da corrida pelo Palácio do Planalto.
articles.summary: Diretor da Quaest e professor da Fundação Getúlio Vargas (FGV), Felipe Nunes avalia momento atual da corrida pelo Palácio do Planalto.
articles.body:
1. Pesquisa Quaest mostra que a eleição continua muito acirrada. Os dois candidatos continuam tecnicamente empatados. Nas nossas estimativas, com 95% de confiabilidade, a intenção de voto em Flávio está entre 43% e 47%. A de Lula, entre 42% e 46%. Indecisos podem chegar a 4%.

Quaest: Flávio Bolsonaro tem 45% e Lula, 44%, em cenário de empate técnico no segundo turno. — Foto: Reprodução/X

2. O quadro quase não se alterou entre as duas rodadas. A distância de 2 pontos passou para 1 ponto, mas essa oscilação na margem de erro não nos permite tirar nenhuma conclusão sobre ‘virada’, ‘mudança’ ou ‘vantagem’.

Evolução das intenções de voto em Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) e Lula (PT) no segundo turno, segundo a Quaest, entre 14 e 21 de outubro. — Foto: Reprodução/X

3. O voto útil de direita captado pela Quaest na última semana do primeiro turno já havia esvaziado o reservatório de votos dos outros candidatos e inflado Flávio. Na pesquisa, esse recall é fundamental para entender a matriz de mudança de voto.

Pesquisa Quaest mostra como os eleitores dizem ter votado para presidente no primeiro turno das eleições de 2026. — Foto: Reprodução

4. A taxa de retenção de voto dos candidatos continua muito alta. Flávio retém 94% e Lula 95% de quem diz ter votado neles no 1º turno. Os 9 milhões de eleitores que votaram em outras alternativas (6%) estão se distribuindo mais para o Flávio (43%), do que para o Lula (37%). No eleitor que diz não ter ido votar ou que votou branco/nulo acontece o inverso: 40% dizem que agora votam em Lula e 36%, em Flávio.

Pesquisa Quaest mostra a transferência de votos do primeiro para o segundo turno entre Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro. — Foto: Reprodução/X

5. Entre os subgrupos, a pesquisa sugere alta estabilidade entre as rodadas. Só há sinal de potencial mudança em um segmento: a vantagem do Lula sobre o Flávio entre beneficiários de programas sociais aumentou, saiu de 29 pp para 37 pp.

Pesquisa Quaest mostra a evolução das intenções de voto em Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro no segundo turno entre beneficiários e não beneficiários do Bolsa Família. — Foto: Reprodução/X

6. Este eleitorado corresponde a 21% da amostra e é politicamente importante por ter sido beneficiado com um aumento do governo. Para além disso, é o segmento em que mais cresceu o medo da volta da família Bolsonaro. Argumento de campanha que pode estar funcionando neste subgrupo.

Quaest mostra o que mais provoca medo entre beneficiários e não beneficiários do Bolsa Família: a reeleição de Lula ou a volta da família Bolsonaro ao poder. — Foto: Reprodução/X

7. O dado mais impressionante da pesquisa, no entanto, é aquele que abre o questionário: no voto espontâneo Flávio e Lula têm o mesmo % de intenção de voto: 40%. O que cresceu da rodada anterior foi a indecisão. Dobrou. Saltou de 7% para 14%.

Evolução das intenções espontâneas de voto para presidente entre 14 e 21 de outubro, segundo a Quaest. — Foto: Reprodução/X

8. Essa indecisão na escolha do candidato de forma espontânea se destaca, especialmente, entre alguns subgrupos. Entre as mulheres, por exemplo, os dois candidatos perderam intenção de voto e a indecisão foi para 17%.

Pesquisa Quaest mostra a evolução das intenções espontâneas de voto para presidente entre homens e mulheres. — Foto: Reprodução/X

9. E entre os independentes, eleitores pragmáticos, não ideológicos, não calcificados, aqueles que decidirão a eleição no próximo domingo, a indecisão saiu de 13% para 31%. Sinalização clara de descontentamento com as opções e com a campanha negativa que vem sendo apresentada.

Quaest mostra as intenções espontâneas de voto em Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro por identificação política dos eleitores. — Foto: Reprodução/X

10. A alta imprevisibilidade desta eleição aparece também no volume de eleitores que ainda pode mudar o voto. No total da amostra, são 10%. Entre eleitores do Lula são 9%, entre eleitores do Flávio são 7%.

Pesquisa Quaest mostra o percentual de eleitores de Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro que consideram sua escolha de voto definitiva ou admitem mudar até o segundo turno. — Foto: Reprodução/X

11. O potencial de voto dos dois candidatos oscilou pra cima. Lula ampliou de 47% para 49% e Flávio de 46% para 48%. Em compensação, a rejeição diminuiu. O não-voto em Lula saiu de 53% para 47%. Flávio saiu de 54% para 52% de rejeição.

Evolução da rejeição e do potencial de voto em Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro, segundo a Quaest. — Foto: Reprodução/X

12. A bala de prata do governo nesses últimos dias, foi o seu maior adversário ao longo dessa campanha: a aprovação! Com o amplo pacote de benesses anunciado, a aprovação de Lula chega ao seu melhor patamar desde 14/ago: 46% aprovam e 47% desaprovam o governo.

Pesquisa Quaest mostra a evolução da aprovação e da desaprovação do governo Lula entre janeiro e outubro de 2026. — Foto: Reprodução/X

13. A Quaest entrevistou 2.154 pessoas entre 17 e 20/out. A margem de erro é de 2 pontos percentuais, com 95% de confiança. Registro no TSE: BR-08535/2026.

Flávio Bolsonaro e Lula em entrevista com Renata Lo Prete — Foto: Globo/ Manoella Mello

articles.title: 'Um tribunal que pretende substituir o debate político trai sua missão', diz presidente do STF | G1
articles.standfirst: Ministro Edson Fachin defendeu que um dos desafios do Judiciário é 'o equilíbrio entre a omissão e o protagonismo'.
articles.summary: Ministro Edson Fachin defendeu que um dos desafios do Judiciário é 'o equilíbrio entre a omissão e o protagonismo'.
articles.body:
O presidente do Supremo Tribunal Federal ( STF ), ministro Edson Fachin , afirmou nesta quarta-feira (21) que a Corte deve buscar sempre encontrar o equilíbrio entre agir diante de violações de direitos fundamentais e evitar interferir nas decisões que cabem ao debate político .

Segundo o magistrado, tanto a omissão quanto o protagonismo podem comprometer a missão do tribunal.

"Um tribunal que se retrai diante de violações de direitos fundamentais trai a sua missão. Mas, um tribunal que pretende substituir o debate político por sua própria vontade também a trai, pois transforma a guarda da Constituição em governo dos juízes", afirmou Fachin.

Ele prosseguiu: "O Estado de Direito exige que se evitem os dois extremos, e a medida entre eles não está prescrita em nenhum manual. Constrói-se, caso a caso, com prudência, coerência e transparência".

Ministro Edson Fachin — Foto: Alejandro Zambrana/STF

O ministro deu a declaração durante discurso de abertura do evento interno “Diálogos com o Supremo”, na sede da Corte, em Brasília.

Fachin também reforçou reflexões que tem feito à frente do tribunal sobre a defesa das instituições democráticas.

"Democracias contemporâneas raramente morrem por golpes abruptos. Corroem-se, muitas vezes, por dentro, e, não raro, por meios aparentemente legais: pela captura gradual das instituições, pelo enfraquecimento dos controles, pela erosão da confiança pública".

O Supremo Tribunal Federal tem sido alvo de críticas por suposta atuação política e extrapolação de suas competências.

As acusações ganharam força em meio a divergências entre ministros e à crise envolvendo o caso Banco Master, levando os candidatos à Presidência, Lula (PT) e Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) que disputam o segundo turno no próximo domingo (25), a defender mudanças no funcionamento do Judiciário.

articles.title: Lula diz que pobre é ‘bom pagador’ e que ‘tem muito rico que gosta de dever’ | G1
articles.standfirst: Presidente deu declaração ao defender perdão de dívidas de microempreendedores. Presidente participou de cerimônia de sanção de medidas para MEIs e assinatura de PEC sobre tarifa zero no transporte.
articles.summary: Presidente deu declaração ao defender perdão de dívidas de microempreendedores. Presidente participou de cerimônia de sanção de medidas para MEIs e assinatura de PEC sobre tarifa zero no transporte.
articles.body:
O presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) afirmou nesta quarta-feira (21) que pessoas pobres são boas pagadoras e disse que há “muita gente rica que gosta de dever”.

A declaração foi dada durante cerimônia de anúncio de lei que perdoa dívidas de microempreendedores individuais (MEIs) e ao transporte público.

Ao defender as medidas para os pequenos empreendedores, Lula afirmou que pessoas de baixa renda valorizam o pagamento de suas dívidas.

“Se tem gente boa pagadora nesse país e gente que gosta de pagar sua dívida é o pobre nesse país”, declarou.

Na sequência, Lula disse que pessoas mais pobres chegam a ficar constrangidas quando estão devendo e usam o dinheiro disponível para quitar os débitos.

“Quando um pobre deve na padaria, ele tem vergonha de passar na porta da padaria, de vergonha de ser cobrado. Quando ele tiver o dinheiro, a primeira coisa que ele faz é pagar, porque tem uma coisa que vale para o povo trabalhador, que é uma coisa chamada honra”, afirmou.

Lula então contrapôs esse comportamento ao de pessoas mais ricas.

“Tem muita gente rica que gosta de dever. Dever é uma coisa charmosa: quanto mais eu devo, melhor. O pobre, não. O pobre fica honrado quando ele não tem dívida, que ele pode andar de cabeça erguida nesse país”, disse.

Lula anuncia medidas em cerimônia no Palácio do Planalto. — Foto: Reprodução/Youtube

A declaração foi dada após Lula tratar do perdão de dívidas de MEIs. Segundo o presidente, o governo decidiu abrir mão dos débitos porque avaliava que parte desses recursos não seria recuperada.

“É um dinheiro que a gente sabia que a gente não ia receber”, afirmou.

Durante o discurso, Lula também defendeu o empreendedorismo e afirmou que mudanças no mercado de trabalho levaram parte da população a buscar alternativas ao emprego tradicional.

“O mundo do trabalho mudou. E as pessoas têm razão em não querer trabalhar para ganhar apenas um pouco”, disse.

Para Lula, quem busca trabalhar por conta própria deve ser valorizado. “Toda pessoa que pensa em trabalhar por conta própria é uma pessoa que merece ser valorizada. Sabe por quê? Porque ela está acreditando nela”, declarou.

O presidente também citou a proposta de concessão de R$ 5 mil para empreendedores e afirmou que o recurso não será um empréstimo.

“É uma doação do governo para que vocês possam começar a vida de vocês de cabeça erguida, sem ficar pedindo favor a ninguém”, disse Lula.

A concessão dos R$ 5 mil não integra a lei sancionada nesta quarta e ainda depende de aprovação do Congresso.

Na mesma cerimônia, Lula assinou a mensagem que encaminha ao Congresso uma proposta de emenda à Constituição (PEC) para financiar a tarifa zero no transporte coletivo urbano.

Durante a cerimônia, o governo anunciou que a proposta prevê a destinação de no mínimo 26,8% do montante global anual das emendas parlamentares para custear a gratuidade.

Em seu discurso, Lula disse esperar que a PEC seja votada ainda neste ano e afirmou que a gratuidade em fins de semana e feriados poderá funcionar como uma primeira experiência, com possibilidade de adoção de novas medidas no futuro caso haja condições fiscais.

articles.title: Trump rallies NC for Republicans as money dries up, ratings favor Democrats
articles.summary: President Donald Trump visited Greenville Tuesday night to rally for struggling Republicans as political watchers change races in favor of Democrats and more...
articles.body:
What started as a disjointed speech in Greenville from President Donald Trump ended as a rallying cry from the president to elect struggling Republican candidates on North Carolina's ballot.

Trump went as far as to promise $5,000 to every adult citizen if Republicans take back the House and Senate — a promise he's made in the past — and to also tie the election results to pending lawsuits by Marines who have suffered serious medical complications from contaminated water at Camp Lejeune.

"Tonight, I'm pleased to announce that my administration has delivered $1 billion in cash settlements to these veterans and their families, most of whom are based here," Trump said.

Trump said if Republicans win the House and Senate he will direct the Department of Justice to settle all remaining legitimate claims as soon as possible.

"If we don't win, there's no money," Trump said. "If we do win, you're getting it."

Gov. Josh Stein, a Democrat, immediately posted on social media in response to Trump's statement.

"Real leaders fight for the people, not for power," Stein said. "To condition doing the right thing by sick North Carolinians on who wins the election is foul."

Andrew Bates, a former spokesman for President Joe Biden and an adviser to former Gov. Roy Cooper's Senate campaign, called Trump's statement "an anti patriotic thing for the president to say."

Trump, standing at Pitt-Greenville Airport, told the audience of around 1,500, according to pool reports, that he came to North Carolina for two reasons: "I want to tell you how bad Cooper is, and I want to tell you how great Michael Whatley is."

Cooper, 69, a Democrat from Raleigh, is running against Whatley, 58, a Republican from Gastonia. And Cooper has led every poll since the two men entered the race in July 2025, often by double digits.

That's led key national Republican groups to pull ad funding from Whatley's campaign and invest in other candidates around the country.

And as the rally was underway, news broke that the No Going Back PAC, a super PAC tied to Trump, pulled out of North Carolina's 11th Congressional District race, Punchbowl News reported.

Only North Carolina's 1st Congressional District, served by Rep. Don Davis, a Democrat from Snow Hill, had originally been expected to be a battleground, and Republican legislators redrew Davis' district to favor a win for their party. Davis is running against former Trump adviser Laurie Buckhout, a Republican from Edenton.

But with Trump's job approval at an all-time low, and Whatley's inability to raise his name recognition, despite having led both the state and national Republican parties, there's been a trickle-down effect to at least five congressional districts among the state's 14.

And that includes the 11th Congressional District, where state Rep. Jennifer Balkcom added her name to the Republican ticket at the last hour after U.S. Rep. Chuck Edwards, a Republican from Flat Rock, withdrew from the race due to a sexual harassment scandal involving congressional employees.

Whatley, Buckhout and Balkcom all spoke on stage both before and during Trump's speech.

The same day, the University of Virginia's Center for Politics changed the 1st and 11th Congressional District ratings from "toss-up" races to "leans Democrat ." Both are in districts that typically are solidly Republican.

Early Republican turnout was down compared to where it stood in 2022, the last midterm election, according to Western Carolina University political science professor Chris Cooper.

State Republican Party Chairman Jason Simmons kicked off Tuesday night's rally by telling the audience to vote Republican up and down the ballot and to bring friends.

"Make sure to go vote, but don't go alone," Simmons said.

At least one person in the audience said she still hadn't made up her mind, even about Trump.

Maggie Lynn Heron-Heidel, who moved to Tarboro six months ago from Connecticut, write dystopian books and said "there are a lot of people who insist Trump is straight out of a dystopian novel."

She said she hadn't made up her mind on Trump or his policies so she came to hear him speak.

And some of her top concerns were rising costs, especially at the grocery store.

Trump didn't address groceries but did talk about gas prices, which have risen as Trump continues a war he started against Iran to stop the country from having nuclear weapons.

Trump said Tuesday night, "This is a very small price to pay for keeping a nuclear weapon away from the world's number one state sponsor of terror."

He promised to lower gas prices again when the war ends.

Glenn Mancher, a Merry Hill resident originally from Brooklyn, New York, drove an hour to attend Tuesday night's rally, wearing a Trump 2028 hat.

"I'd like Trump to finish off the Iranians as quickly as possible," Mancher said. "That would bring down energy prices."

Bates told McClatchy exclusively that Tuesday's rally is a "visceral reminder of Michael Whatley's support for the Iran War that's making gas and diesel prices skyrocket."

"That's on top of the unprecedented cuts to health care Whatley wanted, which are hurting people all over Eastern North Carolina just so billionaires like Elon Musk can pay lower taxes," Bates said.

He called Tuesday's rally "just about the worst message you could take to the Old North State right now."

Trump appeared in North Carolina just 34 days prior and called North Carolina cities "blood-soaked killed fields" leaning into Republican messaging that Cooper was soft on crime because of the release of more than 3,500 prisoners during the COVID-19 pandemic under a legal settlement.

Cooper and other North Carolina officials were sued by civil rights groups during the pandemic after Cooper refused to release half the state's prison population. A judge told North Carolina officials he'd likely side with the civil rights groups and find that the prison conditions were no longer constitutional because of the virus.

To prevent the release of 18,000 inmates, state officials say, they settled and released 3,500. They included DeCarlos Brown on the list of people who were released, despite Brown having already served his full sentence prior to the settlement being agreed upon.

But in August 2025, after police said Brown killed Ukrainian refugee Iryna Zarutska on the light rail in Charlotte, Republicans have used the prison release against Cooper's Senate campaign.

On Tuesday, Trump called Cooper "a fool."

"He's a super liberal fool," Trump said. "I think a fool, because a senator who cares more about shielding murderers from a cough or a virus or something that will not — for the most part these killers were young, and instead of protecting innocent citizens from bloodthirsty killers — then Roy Cooper is the Dumocrat."

Trump signed into law the CARES Act passed by Congress that allowed the release of more than 13,000 federal prisoners into home confinement during the pandemic.

Trump never brought up the CARES Act during Tuesday's speech but said "it's crazy" Cooper could become senator after abiding by the court settlement.

He and Whatley also questioned Cooper's mental acuity, a new line of attack from Republicans against Cooper after The North State Journal published a cease-and-desist demand from the Cooper campaign in response to a reporter from the outlet questioning whether he had a "neurological issue." Cooper's lawyers said Cooper does not, and that to publish anything to the contrary would be defamatory.

Trump turned his attention to Whatley, crediting him for the success of Trump's 2024 campaign. At the time, Whatley was leading the Republican National Committee.

"A lot of people said it's one of the best campaigns ever run," Trump said. "I wanted him to be the guy, and I was right. I called it right. And I think he'll be an even better senator."

Trump handpicked Whatley to succeed Sen. Thom Tillis, a Republican from Huntersville, who got into a public feud with Trump over how Trump's One Big Beautiful Bill would affect North Carolina's Medicaid recipients. That caused Tillis to drop his reelection bid, and Trump to tap Whatley to run against Cooper.

Trump's visit Tuesday night came one day after the vice president traveled to Hendersonville for a similar rally, and exactly two weeks before the election.

Trump said he will likely come to the state again before Nov. 3.

articles.title: Putin agrees to resume three-way talks on Ukraine war with Kyiv and Washington, Kremlin says
articles.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin agreed Wednesday to resume three-way negotiations next month with Washington and Kyiv aimed at ending the war in Ukraine, a...
articles.body:
Russian President Vladimir Putin agreed Wednesday to resume three-way negotiations next month with Washington and Kyiv aimed at ending the war in Ukraine , a Kremlin official said, potentially setting up the first such talks since February.

The Russian leader agreed "in principle" to resume the talks after Nov. 10, Putin foreign affairs adviser Yuri Ushakov told reporters following a meeting in St. Petersburg between Putin and U.S. envoy Steve Witkoff.

The talks will focus on "building a security system for Russia and Ukraine after the conflict ends," Ushakov said.

Witkoff's talks with Putin about Moscow's full-scale invasion of Ukraine took place as U.S. President Donald Trump pushed Kyiv to make a deal that stops the fighting.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has insisted that only a summit of leaders can break the impasse. The two armies remain locked on the battlefield, and the countries pummel each other with daily long-range strikes.

Representatives of the three countries held three rounds of negotiations early this year, meeting twice in Abu Dhabi in January and February, followed by further talks in Geneva in February.

However, little progress was reported beyond exchanges of prisoners of war as Moscow and Kyiv stuck to their longstanding basic demands .

Latest proposals to end the war have little of value, Kremlin says

The discussion in St. Petersburg lasted about three hours, the Kremlin said, and came a day after Witkoff met with Zelenskyy and some European leaders in Norway's capital, Oslo.

The proposals from the Oslo meeting "contained little of real value in the context of resolving the Ukrainian crisis," Ushakov said.

However, he later told Russian state TV that while Moscow isn't "fully satisfied" with the Oslo proposals, they are a step in the right direction.

Witkoff's meetings suggested leaders are keen to bring new momentum to U.S.-led peace efforts , more than 4½ years after the war began. Efforts by the Trump administration since early last year to end the war have made no significant progress.

Zelenskyy said freezing the conflict in Ukraine was the "minimum" required from Russia to bring about an end to the war.

"Right now, we have to freeze, and I think this is (the) real way to end this war," Zelenskyy said in an interview broadcast Wednesday on Fox News.

Witkoff sees 'some degree of momentum' in peace efforts

Witkoff and Putin met at St. Petersburg's Constantine Palace, with Ushakov and Russian presidential envoy Kirill Dmitriev also at the table. Trump's son-in-law, Jared Kushner, joined the discussion via a video link, Ushakov said.

Before the meeting, Witkoff said that there was "some degree of momentum" in talks.

During the meeting, Witkoff and Kushner proposed a three-way meeting with the U.S., Russia and Ukraine at the technical level and shared progress on their talks with Zelenskyy a day earlier, according to a U.S. official familiar with the talks who spoke on condition of anonymity to discuss the private meeting.

Witkoff and Kushner also discussed a postwar economic plan, European security and plans for the upcoming meeting, the official said.

In televised opening remarks, Witkoff thanked Putin for agreeing to send diesel to the U.S., after Trump lifted a ban despite anger from some U.S. lawmakers , adding that the fuel would help reduce prices for American farmers and truckers.

Putin said he was ready to consider prospects for the restoration of U.S.-Russia economic ties and that he was prepared to discuss the U.S.-led conflict with Iran . Moscow stands ready to use its relationship with Tehran to help bring peace, he said.

Ushakov said that "large-scale joint economic projects that offer significant prospects for cooperation" between Russia and the U.S. were discussed in detail with Witkoff.

"Some of these are, in fact, nearing the implementation stage," he said.

In other developments, Russia on Wednesday released a retired American teacher who had been imprisoned on charges of fighting as a mercenary in Ukraine. Witkoff said it appeared to be a goodwill gesture by the Kremlin after Trump asked Putin to free Stephen Hubbard.

Putin also met Wednesday with Chinese Premier Li Qiang, who was in St. Petersburg for talks with other Russian officials, the Kremlin said.

Russia has cultivated its ties with China , and the two countries last month vetoed a U.S. proposal for U.N. experts to keep monitoring sanctions on Iran.

Putin and Witkoff also discussed a possible meeting next month between the Russian, Chinese and U.S. leaders at an economic summit in China, Ushakov said, adding that Beijing is already preparing for it.

Norway's prime minister sees a possible 'new phase' in talks

After his trip to Russia, Witkoff returned for more consultations in Oslo, where he met with Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre at the airport before flying back to the U.S. The meeting lasted just over an hour, Norwegian broadcaster NRK reported.

"I think we may have entered a phase now where the Russians are also looking for opportunities for diplomacy," Støre told the broadcaster. He said the new talks were likely to happen in mid-November.

Asked whether Zelenskyy could accept a border running along the current front line, Støre said: "I don't think Ukraine will ever formally accept it and say that this is the new border. But whether they can live with it is another matter."

Zelenskyy was still in Oslo on Wednesday, where he visited Norway's parliament and met with lawmakers.

Zelenskyy said the talks in Oslo and St. Petersburg included discussion of future security guarantees for Ukraine, the fate of occupied territories , postwar reconstruction and the possibility of a ceasefire.

At the White House on Tuesday, Trump increased the pressure on Zelenskyy to come to an agreement with Russia as relations between the two leaders have soured again .

"We want Zelenskyy to make a deal," Trump told reporters in the Oval Office. "We've given a lot to Ukraine. We've gotten absolutely nothing back except grief, death, tremendous monetary loss."

If that doesn't happen, "I think it's going to be a very bad thing," Trump said.

Amid fears that Washington was turning its back on Ukraine, Zelenskyy said Kyiv is once again receiving early warnings from its partners about incoming Russian missiles, after recent strikes that he said occurred without enough notice from allies.

Russian attacks kill 5 people and wound at least 23 others, Ukraine says

Overnight Russian attacks in Kyiv left three people dead and 12 wounded, while 10 residential buildings were damaged, the city's military administration said.

Energy facilities were targeted in Kyiv and three other cities in Russian attacks early Wednesday, Ukrainian Prime Minister Serhii Koretskyi said. Outside the eastern city of Kharkiv, two people died and 11 others were wounded when drones exploded in a residential area, he said.

The Russian Defense Ministry said that overnight its forces struck a warehouse, an electrical substation and a bulk carrier at sea that was headed to the Ukrainian port of Odesa.

The Russian Defense Ministry reported Wednesday that its air defenses intercepted 373 Ukrainian drones over multiple Russian regions overnight, as well as the illegally annexed Crimean Peninsula and the Black Sea.

articles.title: The House GOP’s imminent decision on the Omar raid
articles.summary: Speaker Mike Johnson has yet to weigh in on the speech-or-debate implications of the raid, though the House has sometimes taken weeks to articulate a positio...
articles.body:
House Republicans have publicly cheered on the Trump administration's investigation of Rep. Ilhan Omar. But underneath the posturing, the raid raises thorny nonpartisan questions about how aggressively Congress wants to defend itself from encroaching federal prosecutors.

The Department of Homeland Security investigators who raided Omar's Washington home last week were searching for evidence related to the Minnesota Democrat's immigration history. But they also emerged in possession of her personal phone, which likely includes a trove of records related to Omar's work at the Capitol — records that both parties have a strong interest in keeping private.

Lawmakers use their cellphones and computers to communicate with aides about upcoming votes, committee hearings and drafting or filing legislation. They text and email colleagues about the work of the House. And they talk to constituents, advisers, attorneys and experts about crucial congressional decisions. The Constitution's "speech or debate" clause makes such material absolutely immune from scrutiny by federal prosecutors, with few exceptions.

The founders adopted those protections to ensure the executive branch could not use its law enforcement power to punish or coerce opponents in Congress. That principle has united Democrats and Republicans, even in this hyperpolarized era.

Speaker Mike Johnson has yet to weigh in on the speech-or-debate implications of the Omar raid, but the House has sometimes taken weeks or months to articulate a position in other recent investigations.

A letter from Omar's attorneys to the Justice Department, reviewed by POLITICO, suggested that the magistrate judge who approved the search ordered investigators to contact the House's top lawyer, Matthew Berry, giving him a chance to intervene on behalf of the institution. Berry's office has been in contact with Trump administration counterparts in recent days, according to two people familiar with the investigation.

The people, who were granted anonymity because they are not authorized to discuss the probe publicly, say investigators have not yet accessed Omar's phone. If they choose to attempt to access it, they must first give Omar a chance to review its contents and assert speech-or-debate protections, with a court ultimately deciding which materials investigators may access.

A representative for the Justice Department declined to comment. Representatives for Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, Johnson and Omar did not respond to requests for comment.

The administration's targeting of Omar comes amid a series of actions the Trump-led Justice Department has taken against Democratic members of Congress: a failed effort to indict Sens. Mark Kelly of Arizona and Elissa Slotkin of Michigan, along with several House members, over comments encouraging members of the military to refuse unlawful orders and criminal charges against Rep. LaMonica McIver for allegedly assaulting an ICE officer during a visit to a New Jersey detention facility.

It also comes amid continued GOP outrage over former special counsel Jack Smith's decision to gather some material related to Republican members of Congress in the aftermath of the 2020 election.

The House's official legal positions are determined by an obscure five-member body known as the Bipartisan Legal Advisory Group, or BLAG. The BLAG is made up of the speaker, majority leader, majority whip, minority leader and minority whip. That panel, always controlled by the majority party, charts the House's course in court. And while most of the BLAG's recent decisions have broken 3-2 along partisan lines, speech-or-debate issues have sometimes resulted in unanimous agreement.

Berry has seen this movie before: In 2022, federal investigators seized the phone of Rep. Scott Perry (R-Pa.) to scrutinize his role in President Donald Trump's bid to subvert the 2020 election. The Justice Department's aggressive action drew a bipartisan response from House leaders, who demanded access to the sealed proceedings to ensure prosecutors didn't cross any constitutional lines. And shortly after Republicans returned to the majority in 2023, Jeffries and Minority Whip Katherine Clark joined GOP leaders and supported Berry's filing of a 36-page brief demanding robust protection of materials seized from lawmakers' cellphones.

That case resulted in a new precedent that treats lawmakers' personal cellphones as an extension of their private offices. It took more than a year of litigation before those investigators, later led by Smith, were able to access a subset of Perry's records that were deemed to fall outside of Congress' constitutional protections.

Stan Brand, a former House counsel who represented Perry in the legal battle against Smith's team, noted that the backdrop of the Omar situation is strikingly similar to one of the most significant constitutional clashes between the House and Justice Department: the 2006 raid of then-Democratic Rep. William Jefferson's congressional office by George W. Bush-era prosecutors. At the time, GOP House leaders joined Democrats in outrage over the raid.

Notably, the DHS investigators who carried out last week's search presented Omar with a "speech or debate" waiver that she refused to sign, according to the letter from Omar's attorneys. Courts have expressed skepticism about whether individual members can waive protections that were intended to safeguard the separation of powers for the entire institution.

"This is just one more example of excess in the Department of Justice under both Democrats and Republicans," Brand said.

Senate Republicans have also accused the Justice Department under President Joe Biden of violating their speech-or-debate protections when Smith subpoenaed their phone records — which don't include the content of texts or emails — from third-party telecom companies like Verizon. One GOP senator is suing Smith and the Justice Department over the matter, and DOJ has since adopted new policies for third-party subpoenas related to members of Congress.

Riley Rogerson and Mia McCarthy contributed to this report.

articles.title: Trump delivers $1 billion to Marines to relieve decades-long suffering of American heroes and their families
articles.summary: Trump announced nearly $1 billion in Camp Lejeune toxic water settlements at a North Carolina rally, ordering the DOJ to resolve all remaining claims.
articles.body: The Trump administration is closing in on $1 billion in payments to American veterans, families and civilian employees who were exposed to toxic drinking water at Marine Corps Camp Lejeune in North Carolina between 1953 and 1987. For many, the payouts would finally rectify a decades-long battle for justice. According to the Department of Justice (DOJ), claimants have received more than $919.7 million since President Donald Trump began his second term in office in January 2025. The administration has paid out about 3,300 people who made claims under the 2022 law. From that year to the beginning of 2025, before Trump retook office, only 459 settlements had been paid, totaling $59.6 million. Payments under the program range from $100,000 to $550,000, depending on the illness. "Tonight I’m pleased to announce my administration has delivered $1 billion in cash settlements to these veterans and their families, in addition to 3.1 billion for the VA and ordering the DOJ to settle all remaining legitimate claims as soon as possible," Trump said at a rally in North Carolina on Tuesday night. "We don’t want to give any to the trial lawyers, we want it all to go to the families." The claims are due to be paid out under a 2022 law, the Sergeant First Class Heath Robinson Honoring our Promise to Address Comprehensive Toxics Act, which includes the Camp Lejeune Justice Act. Under the law, victims who developed cancer or other illnesses from the drinking water on the base are entitled to relief. MILITARY FAMILIES WANT DOJ TO DISTRIBUTE NEARLY $800M FROM FRENCH CEMENT COMPANY FOUND GUILTY OF BRIBING ISIS The Trump administration in March announced that it was making settlements a priority, and made a concerted effort to accelerate the pace of the payouts. Ed Bell is a South Carolina-based attorney who spearheaded the charge to pass the law. He's been an attorney for 44 years, and for half of that time has been fighting for justice for the Camp Lejeune victims. He's the lead counsel on the case, helping victims to get the payouts they're owed. "A lot of these people have been waiting a long time, and quite frankly, I think a lot of them are relieved," Bell told Fox News Digital. "A lot of them feel like the government has finally said, 'we're sorry,' by helping with the settlements, so I think it's very positive." Bell estimates that about 300,000 claims will eventually be paid out, acknowledging that there's a long way to go to completely remedy the wrong that was done. But he was complimentary of the team of people in the Trump administration dedicated to justice. "I have to say, I'm very bullish on what the Department of Justice has been doing," he said, noting that he works closely with Associate Attorney General Stanley Woodward, who he says is "working his tail off" on the settlements. RARE CANCER CASES STRIKE IN CALIFORNIA COMMUNITY AS FAMILIES DEMAND ANSWERS "[Woodward] is excellent, but you have to remember, this case and any resolution involves hundreds and hundreds of details, and it is a laborious process," Bell said. "I am pleased to work with [the DOJ], and I think that eventually we'll get this resolved. I think that's the intent of the Department of Justice." MILITARY FAMILIES DEMAND DOJ DISTRIBUTE NEARLY $800M FROM FRENCH CEMENT COMPANY FOUND GUILTY OF BRIBING ISIS Bell, who took his first case on the Camp Lejeune drinking water contamination in 2007, explained that each settlement is based on the level of harm caused to the victim. So, he explained, someone diagnosed with stage one cancer would ultimately be paid out less than someone who had stage four cancer. "It's a fair system," Bell said. Between 1953 and 1987, three of the base’s eight water systems contained contaminated water. Bell said that even after the government found out the water was toxic, it did nothing, allowing troops to continue drinking the hazardous mix. Pregnant women drank the water, leading to the death of their babies. The contamination was found to cause four incurable diseases, according to Bell. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP The Justice Department and the Department of the Navy launched the "Elective Option" settlement program in 2023. That program is designed as an alternative to litigation and offers quicker payouts to people with qualifying illnesses.

articles.title: Abortion wins elections. Why won’t Democrats say the word?
articles.summary: The midterms offer a key moment to fight back, but are candidates up to the task?
articles.body:
In the weeks leading up to the midterm elections, we have seen attacks on reproductive health care become broader and more dangerous as anti-abortion politicians at the state and federal levels seek to ban access to a key abortion medication nationwide .

The midterms offer a key moment to fight back. But are candidates up to the task?

Back in the day, before MAGA was a thing, Republicans for Choice was a substantial element of the Republican Party. Today, just two Republican senators even purport to support abortion rights. There are none in the House. Federal Election Commission reporting last year for Republicans for Choice disclosed that they raised a paltry $23,000 and ended the year with $4,900 in cash on hand. Republicans for Choice now is more a punchline than a PAC.

Sen. Susan Collins’s (R-Maine) campaign for reelection is downright uncomfortable to watch. While she continues to proclaim she is pro-choice on abortion, she continues to stand by her vote to confirm Justice Brett Kavanaugh and other anti-abortion judges . Finding Republican candidates for office at the state level who support legal abortion can be even more challenging. Vermont’s Gov. Phil Scott (R) might be the only one.

That presents a problem for anyone who believes that protecting reproductive freedom is a priority. We are left with one suitor for our votes: the Democratic Party.

Polling confirms that the majority of Americans believe there should be access to legal abortion nationwide. Support is overwhelming for abortion through the first trimester, and not too shabby for later in pregnancy. Moreover, one in four women will have an abortion in her lifetime. The personal is political.

Yet Democrats shy away from using the “A-word” on the campaign trail.

In Texas, state Rep. James Talarico (D) has been open about his support for abortion rights, noting it as part of his freedom-family-faith platform on his website and underscoring in a recent debate that the Bible does not comment on abortion. But he has not proactively made it an issue of his campaign. Talarico’s opponent, Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton, has been going after reproductive rights like a rabid raccoon since the fall of Roe v. Wade. With fewer than two weeks until the election, Talarico’s support for legal access to abortion should come out of the shadows and into the spotlight.

Texas Gov. Greg Abbott (R), also vehemently anti-abortion, stands in sharp contrast to his challenger for governor, Gina Hinojosa (D). Yet her campaign ad on the issue was — well, not exactly on the issue. Hinojosa spoke about her own pregnancy complications and very difficult loss without acknowledging that her choice would not be an option today in Texas. She left supporters baffled and disappointed.

Coming out in support of abortion rights is a winning strategy. Nearly every ballot measure seeking to expand abortion rights in states across the nation has been overwhelmingly passed and the abortion-rights odds look good on four states’ ballot measures now. Elections in which candidates have emphasized increasing or preserving access to abortion has been a path to victory for them.

New York Gov. Kathy Hochul (D) has a pre-election opportunity to show she has earned her hero’s cape when it comes to reproductive rights. Legislation awaiting her signature would provide protections for New York clinicians to continue to provide an essential abortion and miscarriage management medication — mifepristone — despite the federal government’s attacks on it.

After President Trump appointed three vehemently anti-abortion Supreme Court justices , the Democrat-led house failed to act when they had their chance. We can and should demand more. Because if we don’t, Democrats may not deliver for us either.

We witnessed this recently as California Gov. Gavin Newsom (D), a staunch supporter of abortion rights, disappointingly vetoed a bill that would have kept strong the telemedicine abortion shield law he supported and signed even after he leaves office. We can and should expect more from former Health and Human Services Secretary Xavier Becerra’s (D) campaign .

Now, during the height of election season, government powerbrokers need to prioritize abortion rights. It is a winning strategy that will inspire more voters to turn out at the voting booth. We must be vigilant and not cede ground to an anti-abortion minority that never stops paying attention.

Julie F. Kay, a human rights attorney, is the founder and CEO of Reproductive Futures and co-author of “ Controlling Women: What We Must Do Now to Save Reproductive Freedom. “

articles.title: Socialist primary sweep sparks launch of new resource laying out what’s at stake in 2026
articles.summary: AAF launches "DSA Exposed" website countering Democratic Socialists of America policies from universal healthcare to abolishing the Senate.
articles.body: FIRST ON FOX: With the midterms less than two weeks away and after socialist-backed candidates notched sweeping primary victories, a conservative group is warning the far-left agenda will leave Americans worse off. Advancing American Freedom (AAF) launched "DSA Exposed" on Wednesday. First obtained by Fox News Digital, the website critiques 12 Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) proposals, including universal healthcare, public ownership of major industries, abolishing the Senate and ICE and ending aid to Israel. AAF argues the proposals would reshape American life — and not for the better. Its site examines their potential effects on healthcare, work, housing and the economy. "In many ways, this election is being framed as a referendum on President Trump, but the Democrats deserve just as much scrutiny and more because of what motivates their actual policy preferences," AAF President Tim Chapman told Fox News Digital. REPUBLICANS JUST GOT A POWERFUL NEW PLAYBOOK FOR THE BATTLE FOR CONGRESS. HERE'S WHAT'S INSIDE. In a letter sent to congressional offices Wednesday outlining the new tool, Chapman called the DSA’s agenda "un-American extremism" and urged lawmakers to condemn its "antisemitic rhetoric." "The DSA represents one of the greatest threats to Americans’ life, liberty, and pursuit of happiness in perhaps American history," he wrote. The website also lays out a visual timeline of socialist governments dating back to the 1900s. From the Soviet Union to present-day Cuba, the timeline shows whether each government remained in power or ultimately collapsed. Chapman said the DSA’s biggest issue is its call for greater government involvement. He argued this could have the opposite effect on affordability than intended. "They're going to put more bureaucrats in charge of the economy and this is the thing that's actually dragging down the economy," he said. SOCIALISTS LAUNCH RADICAL PLATFORM TO ABOLISH THE US SENATE Socialism has become increasingly embedded in American politics after several candidates backed by the DSA prevailed in their Democratic primaries this year. Some of the DSA’s most prominent endorsements include Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y., Rep. Rashida Tlaib, D-Mich., New York Assemblywoman Claire Valdez, U.S. House candidate for New York Darializa Avila Chevalier and Pennsylvania state Rep. Chris Rabb. The DSA’s upward momentum has left many Democrats questioning the future of the party and whether it could shift further to the left. An October Fox News Poll found 32% of voters view socialism favorably, up five points from a year ago, while a March poll found 53% of voters under 30 favored moving away from capitalism toward socialism. Chapman said "a pendulum swing" has left young Americans with "great frustration" over both parties’ handling of the economy. "Right now, you're having populist politics on the right, and you're having populist on the left and both are massively failing when it comes to the economy," he said. YOUNG SWING-STATE VOTERS COZY UP TO DEMOCRATIC SOCIALISTS, SAY PARTY ESTABLISHMENT MUST ‘LEARN’ FROM DSA WINS He said both parties need to do better to prevent an "opening" for socialism and accused Democratic leaders of being hesitant to distance themselves from DSA-aligned policies for fear of losing their party’s base. "The answer is not to give the authority to the democratic socialists on the left, because they'll actually drive it further into the hole," he said. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP As voters head to the polls in November, Chapman hopes the website offers a "deep dive" into socialist platforms and how they stack up against Americans’ priorities. "Even though they may be a minority of the party, they are the energy within the party," Chapman said. "They’re the beating heart of the movement and I think that the leadership of the party will probably kowtow to that base energy."

articles.title: Trump on remarks about GOP senator’s ‘a‑‑’: ‘This guy’s a monster!’
articles.summary: President Trump on Tuesday again complimented the backside of Sen. Jon Husted (R-Ohio), something he has done multiple times on the campaign trail as the midterms near. “I looked at his a‑‑, and then I looked at his legs, and my — I said, ‘His a‑‑ is like, it’s like a pile of muscle.’ Then…
articles.body:
President Trump on Tuesday again complimented the backside of Sen. Jon Husted (R-Ohio), something he has done multiple times on the campaign trail as the midterms near.

“I looked at his a‑‑, and then I looked at his legs, and my — I said, ‘His a‑‑ is like, it’s like a pile of muscle.’ Then I looked at his legs, and I said, ‘Man, his feet are big,’” Trump said during a rally in North Carolina, talking about Husted, who is locked in a tight race with former Sen. Sherrod Brown (D-Ohio).

“Then I looked at his shoulders, and I tapped him on the shoulder, and it actually hurt my hand. It was like a piece of steel. I said, ‘This guy’s a monster,’” the president added.

Trump made similar remarks about Husted’s build at a rally in Ohio a little more than a week ago .

Trump regularly remarks on the appearances of women at rallies and elsewhere, joking he could be “canceled” for the compliments. His comments about men’s physiques have raised the eyebrows of commentators on both sides of the political spectrum.

Comedy Central “Daily Show” host Michael Kosta poked fun at Trump over his Husted comments, saying on Tuesday’s show the president should “find a man” and “take him dancing in your big gay ballroom.”

Fox News host Jesse Watters remarked on similar comments from Trump last week about Husted.

“Trump says a lot of stuff we all think and we don’t say,” Watters said on “The Five.” “Sometimes it sounds a little gay. He can get away with it because he’s straight.”

The president’s comments on Tuesday came two weeks out from Election Day. The Ohio Senate battle is among a handful of Democratic pickup opportunities with headwinds blowing hard against Republicans.

Trump’s approval numbers are at record lows as voters are angry about the war in Iran and the resulting rise in gas prices and overall inflation. Corruption in government is also a top concern down the midterm homestretch.

The nonpartisan political handicapper Cook Political Report rates the Husted-Brown match-up as a “toss-up,” and Decision Desk HQ says Brown has a 53 percent chance of locking down the Senate seat .

articles.title: Democrats hold 10-point advantage ahead of midterms: Survey
articles.summary: The Democratic Party is holding a 10-point advantage over Republicans on the generic ballot less than two weeks from the 2026 midterms, according to a new survey. The CNN/SSRS poll found that 49 percent of respondents chose Democrats when asked to choose “which party’s candidate would you vote for in your Congressional district,” while 39…
articles.body:
The Democratic Party is holding a 10-point advantage over Republicans on the generic ballot less than two weeks from the 2026 midterms, according to a new survey.

The CNN/SSRS poll found that 49 percent of respondents chose Democrats when asked to choose “which party’s candidate would you vote for in your Congressional district,” while 39 percent picked Republicans — the widest margin seen in the poll since just before the 2020 election.

The advantage comes from strong support from traditional pillars of the Democratic coalition, including Black respondents siding with Democrats by a 70-point margin and Latino respondents by a 40-point margin.

For voters who rated the economy as their top concern, 46 percent picked Democrats and 37 chose the GOP, with Democrats also being viewed as the party better equipped to deal with the economy and cost of living.

When asked what would happen if Democrats regained control of Congress, 41 percent of respondents believed the country would be better off, 37 percent responded it would be worse off and 22 percent said it would be no different.

This comes as Sabato’s Crystal Ball, a nonpartisan election handicapper, shifted 28 House races in Democrats’ direction. When adding up the seats Crystal Ball says are either safe, likely or leaning toward one party, the new projections put Democrats above the 218 seats needed for a House majority.

Decision Desk HQ (DDHQ), The Hill’s partner, also forecast Democrats as likely winning the House , rating the party as having a 77 percent chance of regaining control of the chamber. In the Senate, DDHQ gives Democrats a 55 percent chance of taking control .

The poll also found President Trump’s approval rating at a record low of 32 percent, just 1 point below its next lowest point in September.

Trump’s approval rating has plummeted in the months since he authorized strikes on Iran, with the ensuing war leading to rising gas prices nationwide following Iran’s effective shutdown of the Strait of Hormuz.

Though he has sought to ease prices through his Russian diesel deal , among other policy solutions , the average cost of gas in the U.S. hit $4.26 per gallon on Wednesday — almost $1.21 more than the average at this time last year, according to AAA .

The CNN/SSRS poll was conducted Oct. 15-18 among 1,701 respondents. The margin of error was 2.9 percentage points.

articles.title: Ramaswamy doubles down on ad of Acton's estranged mother with $4M buy
articles.summary: Republican gubernatorial candidate Vivek Ramaswamy is doubling down on a controversial ad featuring his opponent's estranged mother with a $4 million buy.
articles.body:
Republican gubernatorial candidate Vivek Ramaswamy is doubling down on a controversial ad featuring his opponent's estranged mother with a $4 million buy.

The ad, which leaked Oct. 19, features the estranged mother of Democratic candidate Amy Acton accusing the candidate of lying about her upbringing. Acton hasn't spoken to her mother since 1978, when her stepfather, Cledith Arthur, was accused of sexually abusing her as a child.

Acton's brother, Philip Stearns, and court records reviewed by the statehouse bureau back up Acton's account of a childhood filled with abuse, neglect and at times, homelessness. Acton's mother, Donna Arthur, lost custody of her two children and left Ohio with Cledith before the rape case against him could be resolved.

"It's not surprising that Vivek Ramaswamy has stooped to such a despicable low as to attempt to turn the sexual abuse Amy endured at 12 years old from our birth mother's husband into a political talking point," Stearns said.

But Ramaswamy is airing that ad anyway. The Republican candidate said people close to Acton, including a mother she has not spoken to in 48 years, have urged Ohioans not to vote for her.

"This is part of a pattern of someone else who appears to know her well who says the same thing, and I do think that it's important for voters to take all of that into account," Ramaswamy told the statehouse bureau.

The ad features Acton's estranged mother, Donna Arthur, urging voters not to pick Acton for governor.

"If you think she'll make your life better, you're fooling yourself," Arthur said in a 60-second ad cut by the Ramaswamy campaign. Ramaswamy said Acton's mother wasn't paid to appear in the spot.

The ad is at least the second time Arthur has publicly accused her daughter of lying. Arthur detailed concerns about Acton's backstory to an anti-abortion group in 2020 while Acton was serving as state health director.

Ramaswamy's campaign confirmed it will spend $4 million on the spot before Election Day, Nov. 3.

What does the record show about Acton's childhood?

Acton detailed her troubled home life and her mother's neglect in a Youngstown Vindicator article published in August 2019. She described living in "18 or so" homes, including one unfinished basement, before turning 12. She recalled Arthur's many boyfriends and their frequent moves. At one point, they lived in a tent outside of Youngstown, Acton told the Vindicator.

According to Acton, the situation escalated when her stepfather sexually abused her at age 12. Austintown Police arrested Cledith Arthur in summer 1978 for the rape of a 12-year-old girl "following an investigation initiated by the girl's father," the Youngstown Daily Vindicator reported at the time .

Cledith Arthur left the state before the case could be resolved. A warrant was issued for his arrest in October 1978 and December 1981, according to court records provided to the statehouse bureau. A records request has been filed with the Mahoning County Common Pleas Court, and they are working to pull records on the case from 1978.

"I received a lot of abuse, but Amy always got the worst of it. She continued to receive that abuse because she knew she had to protect me from that, and if she hadn't done that, who knows where I would have ended up," Stearns said.

Acton's campaign launched a response ad featuring her brother talking about how Acton protected him during their difficult childhood. Acton also addressed the ad on her social media:

"Growing up in Youngstown, my brother Phil and I endured abuse, hunger, and neglect − even spending one winter homeless living in a tent. We were often kept in a dark basement, were frequent-fliers with child protective services, and lived in fear of our birth mother's violent and erratic temper," Acton said in a statement. "Between the ages of 10 and 12, I was sexually abused by her husband, while my birth mother did nothing to protect me. I've always known that she was deeply sick and unwell, and it's sad to see Vivek Ramaswamy exploit her all for his own political gain."

"Eventually, I confided in my father and stepmother, and we were removed from that situation. My birth mother's husband was arrested, charged with rape, and indicted by a grand jury. At 12 years old, I testified in court. I haven't seen my birth mother since that day in 1978. She and her husband fled the state and he was declared a fugitive," she wrote.

State government reporter Jessie Balmert can be reached at jbalmert@usatodayco.com or @jbalmert on X .
